about: Nimble Robotics is a San Francisco AI robotics company building autonomous robots for e-commerce fulfillment, including its Nimble Pick robots and fulfillment systems, with customers among large retailers and logistics providers. Crunchbase shows about $221 million in funding. B2B, with limited public awareness outside logistics.

about: Elvie is a London femtech company, founded in 2013 by Tania Boler, known for the Elvie Pump, a quiet wearable breast pump, and the Elvie Trainer pelvic floor device, sold to mothers via retail and direct online. It has raised about $190 million from investors including Octopus and Kindred. Elvie entered administration in 2025 and its assets were sold to Chiaro. Consumer brand with strong awareness among new mothers in the UK and US.

Fivetran, based in Oakland, California, sells automated data integration software that moves data from business applications and databases into cloud warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks. Customers are enterprises and data teams, and revenue is usage-based subscriptions. It was founded in 2012, was valued at 5.6 billion dollars in 2021, and has raised about $850 million in funding. It merged with dbt Labs in 2025. It is B2B and well known in data engineering but not among consumers.

Nxera is a Singapore based data centre operator, offering digitalisation, cloud and colocation services, according to Crunchbase, with recorded funding of about $800 million. It is understood to be the data centre arm of Singtel, branded Nxera in 2024 with sites across Asia Pacific. Customers are enterprises, hyperscalers and AI workloads. It is a B2B infrastructure brand with limited consumer visibility, though backed by a large telecom parent.

about: BlueVoyant is a New York based cybersecurity company that provides managed detection and response, third-party risk management, and threat intelligence services to enterprises. It was founded in 2017 by former Israeli and US intelligence and corporate security executives and has raised around $665 million-equivalent in funding according to this record. Customers are mid to large enterprises and financial firms, paying subscription and service fees. It is a B2B security brand with limited public awareness.

about: Northern Data Group is a Frankfurt based provider of high-performance computing infrastructure for AI, offering GPU cloud services (Taiga Cloud), Ardent data centers and Peak Mining crypto operations. Customers are AI developers and enterprises. It was listed on the Frankfurt exchange (NB2) and was set to be acquired by Rumble in a 2025 deal. Funding shown is around 575 million euros. It is a B2B infrastructure operator with limited consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Northern Data builds and offers global infrastructure solutions...

about: Tonal is a San Francisco based maker of a wall-mounted smart home gym that uses electromagnetic resistance and AI to coach strength training, sold with a monthly membership of workout programmes. It sells direct to consumers through its website and retail partners, and has raised around $580 million, valuing it at 1.6 billion dollars in 2021. Founded in 2015, it has had a large consumer advertising presence and athlete partnerships including athletes in the NBA and NFL.

Aleph Alpha is a Heidelberg, Germany artificial intelligence company that developed large language models and sovereign AI tools for enterprises and governments, including the Luminous models, and later pivoted towards AI operating systems and services. It was founded in 2019 by Jonas Andrulis, with investors including Schwarz Group, Bosch and SAP-linked groups. Funding shown is about $534 million. It is a B2B European AI company, known in the tech sector and in German policy circles, with little consumer awareness.

Higgsfield is an AI start-up for generative video tools, offering creators AI image-to-video and cinematic camera controls for social media content, with products used by marketers and creators. The Crunchbase entry shows funding of about $538 million, though its location is not given and the text is unclear. This seems to be a very recent company, with a growing profile among creators. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

I-TRACING is a Courbevoie, France cybersecurity services company offering audit, consulting, managed security services and identity protection to large organisations in Europe and beyond. It is part of the Ardian-backed cyber platform following a 2020s ownership change and has hundreds of staff. Funding recorded is about 500 million euros. It is a B2B specialist with strong recognition among IT security buyers in France but no consumer visibility.

about: YipitData is a New York based alternative data and research firm that collects data from web, transaction and other sources to provide analytics on companies and sectors, sold as subscriptions to hedge funds, asset managers and corporates. Founded in 2008, it counts many large investment funds as clients and has raised a major investment from Carlyle in 2021, with funding around $492 million. It is a B2B brand with little public awareness.

DeepRoute.ai is a Shenzhen, China autonomous driving company founded in 2019, developing advanced driver assistance and urban navigation systems, using vision-based and lidar-supported technology, with partners including Great Wall Motor. It sells to automakers who put its software in vehicles. Funding shown is around $450 million. It is a B2B technology supplier, with limited consumer brand awareness but notable visibility in the Chinese auto technology sector.

Redwood Software is a Vienna, Virginia (US) enterprise automation company, offering workflow and job scheduling software for finance, IT and supply chain, such as RunMyJobs and Finance Automation. Customers are large organisations in many industries, and it has a worldwide presence and offices in Europe. It is owned by private equity firms, with funding recorded of about 315 million dollars. It is a B2B software brand with moderate recognition in enterprise IT.
cb_desc: Redwood Software is an international company...

about: Juniper Square is a San Francisco software company providing fund administration, investor relations, accounting and marketing platform for private markets, in particular real estate and alternative asset managers. Customers are general partners of funds, and it connects them with limited partners. Founded in 2014, it was valued at 1.1 billion dollars in 2021 and has raised about $371 million including a 2025 round. It is a B2B software brand with little public awareness.

Instabase is a San Francisco AI company providing a platform for extracting, understanding and automating complex document and unstructured data work, used by banks, insurers and governments for processes such as loan and claims processing. Founded in 2015, it had a large 2021 round at around 2 billion dollars valuation and has raised about $292 million. It sells to large enterprises. It is a B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

Sesame is a San Francisco AI start-up building lifelike conversational voice assistants and smart glasses, known for its Maya and Miles voice demos released in 2025 and its work on natural-sounding speech. Founded by Oculus co-founder Brendan Iribe and Ankit Kumar, it raised a $250 million round in 2025 led by Sequoia and Spark, with total funding of about $308 million. It is a young consumer AI company with a high tech-press profile.

wiki.title: Sesame
wiki.what: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds
wiki.text: Sesame is a plant in the genus Sesamum, also called benne. Numerous wild relatives occur in Africa and a smaller number in India. It is widely naturalized in tropical regions around the world and is cultivated for its edible seeds, which grow in pods. World production in 2024 was 6.7 million tonnes, with India, Myanmar, and Sudan as the largest producers.

about: MaintainX is a San Francisco company offering a mobile-first maintenance and operations platform (CMMS/EAM) for industrial frontline workers, with work orders, checklists, inspections and AI assistance. Customers include manufacturing, food, energy and hospitality companies such as Duracell and Univar. Founded in 2018, it was valued at 2.5 billion dollars in 2024 and has raised about $254 million. It is a B2B software brand, with ads aimed at industrial users, and little consumer awareness.

Tailscale is a Toronto based software company offering a secure private network for devices and teams, built on WireGuard, so that laptops, servers and cloud resources connect without VPN configuration. It is used by developers and companies, with a free tier for individuals. Founded in 2019 by Avery Pennarun, David Crawshaw and others, it raised a 160 million dollar Series C in 2025 and has total funding of around $276 million. It is a B2B and prosumer technology brand known among developers.

Aleo is a San Francisco blockchain company building a privacy-focused layer one network that uses zero-knowledge proofs, so developers can build private applications. It launched its mainnet in 2024, and its Leo programming language is used for smart contracts. Founded in 2019, it raised a 200 million dollar Series B in 2022 led by Kora Management, with total funding around $249 million. It is a crypto infrastructure project with a profile in developer and crypto circles, not a consumer brand.

Buildots is an Israeli construction technology company, based in Tel Aviv, using AI and computer vision with 360 cameras on hard hats to track construction progress against plans automatically. Customers are building contractors and developers in Europe, North America and the Middle East, and it has raised close to 300 million dollars from backers such as Lightspeed and Future Fund. Founded in 2018. B2B software with limited public awareness.

CodeRabbit is a US developer tools start-up, based in San Francisco, offering an AI code review assistant that automatically reviews pull requests on GitHub and GitLab. It sells team subscriptions to software companies and has raised over 200 million dollars, including a 2025 round that valued it at about 550 million dollars. B2B with strong awareness among developers and none among the general public.

Emergent is an AI-powered software creation platform which Crunchbase places in Pleasanton, California. The input describes it as letting users create software with AI and shows funding of about 230 million dollars. Its customers, scale and ownership are not supported by the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Euclyd is a Dutch AI chip and infrastructure start-up based in Eindhoven designing hardware to run AI workloads efficiently. It has raised about 200 million dollars according to the input. Early-stage deep-tech with B2B customers and no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Gravis Robotics is a Swiss robotics company, based in Zurich and spun out of ETH Zurich, developing autonomous technology for heavy construction machines such as excavators, so they can work with little human supervision. Customers are construction and earthmoving firms. It has raised about 223 million dollars per the input, which should be checked. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Linear is a US software company based in San Francisco that sells a project and issue tracking tool, popular with software teams for speed and design, covering issues, projects, cycles and roadmaps. It has raised over 200 million dollars at a valuation above 1.2 billion dollars and is used by companies such as Vercel and Ramp. Founded in 2019. B2B with strong developer brand awareness and none among consumers.

Matic Robots is a US home robotics company based in Mountain View, California, that makes an autonomous home robot vacuum and mop using vision-only navigation, with no cloud dependence. Founded by former Google X and Tesla engineers, it sells to consumers and has raised about 227 million dollars. Early-stage consumer hardware brand with low awareness.
